title: The Fathers on Nahum
rules: Larry Sanger's rules for Deep Dive Bible commentary editions (emails of 8 and 9 Nov 2026): comments of at most 6 adjacent verses (Selected at most 3); cuts marked with an ellipsis; square brackets for editorial additions only; paragraphs added; one-sentence capsule no longer than 40% of the comment. Every word outside brackets is Via Patrum's published translation, checked by script.
scope: Church Fathers (all died by 749) in works published on viapatrum.org as of 9 Nov 2026.

comments.capsule: God often punishes sinners only here, since the Lord will not avenge twice for the same.
comments.comment: For though God often either exacts accounts from sinners only here and not also there — according to “the Lord will not avenge twice for the same” (Nahum 1:9) — or forbears in the present age without also granting forgiveness from there, of such people he says the punishment is indelible and without pardon both here and there.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria

comments.capsule: Christ breathing the Spirit on his disciples after the resurrection fulfils Nahum's words about one who breathes into the face.
comments.comment: …Christ, after the resurrection, breathing into the faces of the disciples, was reclaiming and sanctifying what was corrupted by human disobedience, and said: 'Receive Holy Spirit' (John 20:22); fulfilling the prophecy of Nahum, which relates the thing happening as if already done, through the unbridled desire for the immeasurable beauty of the matter: 'The one who breathes into your face has ascended from the earth, and is lifting you out of tribulation' (Nahum 2:1).
comments.selected_reason: Shows how the verse about breathing into the face was read as the giving of the Spirit.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Nineveh's leaders are fettered so that they cannot freely do forbidden things, for being hindered from iniquity is good.
comments.comment: …it is said to Nineveh: 'And upon your glorious things they shall cast a lot, and all your magnates shall be bound in fetters' (Nahum 3:10), so that they might not do the forbidden things with easy release and hands not hindered; for it is for good to be hindered by 'hands entwined with iniquities.'
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Nineveh thought much of her defenses, but the prophet says her strongholds will fall like figs into the mouth of one eating.
comments.comment: Regarding Nineveh, being taken to mean 'becoming beautified,' she was thinking greatly of those things she had constructed in defenses and unassailable garrisons, which the destroyer of such things says: 'And you will be drunken and will be seen as a wanton, and you will seek for yourself a standing against enemies. Your strongholds will have the purposes of figs, and if they are shaken, they will fall into the mouth of one eating.' (Nahum 3:11-12).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind
